name: Joah
overview: Joah was a male figure known primarily for being sent by King Josiah to oversee the repair of the house of the Lord. Scripture does not specify his tribal affiliation or other personal details beyond this significant task. His role highlights his trusted position in the religious reforms during Josiah's reign.
namesAndTitles: The name Joah means 'YHWH is brother,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord's closeness or kinship. This proper name is recorded in 2 Chronicles 34:8 and was not given directly by God but carries a meaningful connection to the divine name.
familyAndRelationships: Joah is explicitly identified as the father of Joahaz in 2 Chronicles 34:8. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide further information about his family or other relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Joah's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his role in the restoration of the temple under King Josiah's reforms. Being entrusted with repairing the house of the Lord underscores his involvement in the spiritual renewal of Judah and the preservation of true worship. His mention in 2 Chronicles 34:8 situates him within a critical moment of covenant renewal and dedication to God's commands.
